Por qué una placa y no un horno: Why a plate and not an oven
Soldar componentes SMD con cautín funcio: Soldering SMD parts with an iron works until a QFN or a row of 0402s shows up. Solder paste solves that, but it needs disciplined heat: rise without burning, hold for the right time and cool down.
**HotPlate** es mi respuesta: una placa: **HotPlate** is my answer: a heating plate with two PTC heaters, a PT100 sensor and an ATmega16 that runs a **Soldering Profile** of up to four steps. No more watching a thermometer and switching off by hand.
Un ciclo completo con un solo gesto: A full cycle with a single press
Pulsas **RUN** y el programa HEAT recorr: You press **RUN** and the HEAT program walks the whole profile in order:
Rampa a la temperatura de cada escalón y: Ramp to each step's temperature and a hold from 30 s to 60 min. Steps only rise or stay level.
Aviso de fin con pitidos y el calor ya a: End alert with beeps and the heat already off.
Enfriamiento con aire hasta la temperatu: Air cooling down to the minimum temperature.
Salidas apagadas al arrancar, ante un fa: Outputs off at boot, on a sensor fault or when the maximum temperature is reached.
HotPanel: temperatura en grande y una pe: HotPanel: big temperature and one knob
La pantalla ST7920 de 128×64 muestra la: The 128×64 ST7920 screen shows the temperature, the phase, the current step with its setpoint and the elapsed time. With the encoder you edit the four ramps and the wait without plugging anything in. When the computer takes over, HotPanel says so and locks local control.
Una placa de aluminio tiene inercia: si: An aluminium plate has inertia: cut the heat when you hit the setpoint and it keeps rising. The controller is a **predictive PI**: it follows a reference rising at 1.2 °C/s and computes the error against the temperature expected 15 s ahead.
La salida se aplica al relé de estado só: The output drives the solid-state relay (MOC3021 + BT136) as on-time within 1.5 s windows, with anti-windup. If power stays at 95 % for 3 minutes without reaching the target, it cuts off and reports it: an unreachable setpoint does not keep heating forever.

Adivinar Kp y Ki a ojo es lento. El prog: Guessing Kp and Ki by eye is slow. The **autotune** program makes the plate oscillate around a setpoint with bang-bang heat, measures the amplitude and period of the oscillation and computes a PI with **Ziegler–Nichols**.
Las ganancias se guardan en la EEPROM so: The gains are written to EEPROM only when tuning finishes cleanly. In the run shown, at 150 °C and five cycles, it produced Kp 78 and Ki 6.
Traza de autoajuste: la temperatura osci: Autotune trace: temperature oscillates around 150 °C while the heater switches between 0 and 100 %

Es una aplicación de escritorio en Pytho: It is a Python desktop app that talks to HotPlate over USB. It edits the profile, starts HEAT or autotune, plots temperature against setpoint and power live, marks every phase change and exports the log to CSV. Everything HotPanel does not expose (limits, hold bands, air at the end, gains) is set here and stored on the device.
HotPlate Studio en la pestaña HEAT con e: HotPlate Studio on the HEAT tab with the profile, the status and the live curve
Studio no tiene privilegios especiales:: Studio has no special privileges: it uses the same protocol as any script. Five AT verbs (`MODE`, `RUN`, `STOP`, `CFG`, `STAT`) at 19200 baud and one `$HP` frame per second with temperature, phase, setpoint and power.
Cinco corridas HEAT y dos de autoajuste: Five HEAT runs and two autotune runs were saved and feed a regression test that runs on the computer. The numbers, unpolished:
Enfriamiento con aire: de 130 a 50 °C en: Air cooling: from 130 to 50 °C in 12 to 17 minutes.
Última traza HEAT: escalones de 150, 165: Latest HEAT trace: 150, 165 and 175 °C steps with heater power
Todo corre en un ATmega16 a 8 MHz: lectu: Everything runs on an ATmega16 at 8 MHz: MAX31865 reads, control, profile, screen and USB, with a cooperative scheduler and no blocking waits. The firmware uses **16,382 of 16,384 bytes** of flash.
Con ese margen, cada función nueva se mi: With that margin, every new feature is measured with `make size` and logged in a budget. The rule is simple: the approved interface and the thermal core are never sacrificed to fit something else.
Falta la prueba que importa: una traza c: The test that matters is still pending: a full trace above 183 °C, the melting point of Sn63/Pb37, with a real board on top. For lead-free solder (≈ 217 °C) we first need to measure whether the plate gets there under load.

kLog: los logs se quedan en tu servidor: kLog: the logs stay on your server
Una plataforma self-hosted para capturar: A self-hosted platform to capture, store and query events from apps and IoT, with REST ingest and GraphQL management.
Un lugar propio para los eventos: A place of your own for events
Cuando una API, una web o un gateway de: When an API, a website or a sensor gateway emits an event, the usual path is to send it to someone else's service. **kLog** starts the other way: an open-source platform you install on your own server. The logs stay home and the cost does not depend on a per-gigabyte plan.
No es un montaje obligatorio de Grafana,: It is not a required assembly of Grafana, Loki and Prometheus. It is one application: a console, an API and a worker, with Postgres and Redis behind them.
Cinco piezas, cada una con su proceso: Five pieces, each with its own process
El workspace agrupa repositorios hermano: The workspace groups sibling repositories. Each one starts on its own and they talk over URLs:
**api**: Go. GraphQL para consultar y ad: **api**: Go. GraphQL to query and manage. REST only for ingest and health.
**ingest**: worker Go que consume la col: **ingest**: a Go worker that consumes the Redis queue `klog:jobs:default`.
**Postgres** guarda el plano de control: **Postgres** stores the control plane and each tenant's events. **Redis** carries the queues.
Los contratos compartidos viven aparte,: The shared contracts live apart, in Go (`klog/goshared`) and TypeScript (`@klog/shared`).
Escribir por REST, leer por GraphQL: Write over REST, read over GraphQL
Un servicio o un dispositivo no abre Gra: A service or a device does not open GraphQL. It sends `POST /v1/ingest/{tenantId}/events` with a project API token. The token looks like `klog_<prefix>_<secret>`: the secret is shown once and the database keeps only its hash.
La consola, el alta de tenants y la cons: The console, tenant setup and queries use GraphQL. The live tail (`eventLive`) exists as a contract and starts off: it needs a user session and `LIVE_TAIL_ENABLED=true`. An API token does not authenticate GraphQL.
Cada cliente en su schema: Each customer in its own schema
Postgres usa un `BIGINT` interno y expon: Postgres uses an internal `BIGINT` and exposes a UUIDv7 `public_id`. GraphQL and REST only accept that public identifier.
El plano de control (`control`) guarda u: The control plane (`control`) stores users, sessions, tenants, roles and permissions. Each customer's events live in their own schema, created from a template (`tenant_template`). A table change is written once and propagated, without mixing two organizations' data.
El acceso no es un único rol de administ: Access is not a single administrator role. There are members, permissions and grants per resource. The session cookie is HttpOnly (`klog_access`) or a bearer JWT; the token does not carry roles inside: the API resolves them against the stored session. On ingest, the project token enters as the `device` role and can only write to that project's applications.
La API valida el token, comprueba que la: The API validates the token, checks that the application belongs to the project and stores the event. Later work —rules, transforms, webhooks— goes to Redis. The `ingest` worker consumes it without holding the response. API health is on `:3100`; the worker's is on `:3001`.
La búsqueda de la v1 está definida sobre: v1 search is defined on the same Postgres: full text, paths inside the JSON and typo tolerance with `pg_trgm`. Meilisearch stays a later read index, not a requirement to start.
Lo que ya se puede recorrer de punta a p: What you can already walk end to end is the short path: register, create the application, send an event with the token and see it in the console. Transforms, webhooks with retry and fuzzy search are the next stretch, not a hidden dependency.
Placa calefactora que ejecuta un Solderi: A hot plate that runs a Soldering Profile of up to four steps, with predictive PI control and a desktop app.
Soldar SMD con cautín se acaba cuando ap: Soldering SMD with an iron runs out when a QFN shows up. HotPlate melts the paste on a curve: wait, rise, hold each plateau and shut off. The paste does not depend on someone watching the thermometer.
El cerebro es un ATmega16 a 8 MHz. Mide: The brain is an ATmega16 at 8 MHz. It measures with a PT100 and a MAX31865, and switches two PTC heaters through a solid-state relay (MOC3021 + BT136). The local face is HotPanel, a 128×64 ST7920 and an encoder.
HotPlate Studio, en el computador, habla: HotPlate Studio, on the computer, talks over USB at 19200 baud: it edits the profile, starts the cycle or autotune, draws the curve and exports CSV. The same AT protocol works from a script. The firmware fits exactly: 16,382 of 16,384 bytes of flash.
El relato del ciclo, las trazas y el aut: The cycle, the traces and the autotune are in the tutorial [HotPlate: SMD reflow without an oven](https://kriverdevice.krisskira.com/tutoriales/hotplate-reflow-smd). The code, the KiCad PCB and the enclosure are in the [repository](https://github.com/krisskira/smd-soldering-hotplate). It uses mains power: that is on you.
Plataforma self-hosted para ingerir even: A self-hosted platform to ingest events from apps and IoT, store them per tenant and query them from a console.
kLog captura logs y eventos sin entregar: kLog captures logs and events without handing them to a third party. The offer is data sovereignty and a predictable cost against a hosted observability service, with one application instead of a Grafana assembly.
La API en Go separa el trabajo: REST par: The Go API splits the work: REST for `POST /v1/ingest/{tenantId}/events` and health; GraphQL for users, tenants, permissions and queries. Postgres splits the control plane and one schema per tenant. Redis carries the queue the worker consumes.
El acceso distingue personas y dispositi: Access distinguishes people and devices. The session is an HttpOnly cookie or a JWT; a device uses a project API token that can only write to its applications. The public identifier is a UUIDv7.
El recorrido de la ingesta, el token y l: The ingest path, the token and the planned search are in the tutorial [kLog: the logs stay on your server](https://kriverdevice.krisskira.com/tutoriales/klog-registros-que-se-buscan).
KiCad IA: describes el circuito en un ch: KiCad IA: you describe the circuit in a chat and the schematic comes out with the parts and footprints from your own libraries. No invented components, and nothing already on the board gets broken.
Un LED con su resistencia, un regulador: An LED with its resistor, a regulator with its capacitors, a USB-C connector with its protection. These blocks get drawn again and again, and every time you have to find the symbol, assign the footprint and wire the nets by hand.
**KiCad IA** es un plugin para KiCad 10: **KiCad IA** is a KiCad 10 plugin that changes that part: you describe the circuit in a chat and it writes the open project's schematic. The parts come from the libraries you already have configured, not from a separate catalog.
Del botón a la placa: From the button to the board
En el editor de PCB aparece el botón **K: The PCB editor shows a **KiCad IA** button. Pressing it opens the chat in the browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. The full path:
Eliges el modelo en Ajustes: Google Gemi: You pick the model in Settings: Google Gemini, local Ollama, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible URL.
Describes el circuito, o pulsas el **＋**: You describe the circuit, or press the **＋** in the text field for a quick action.
Cierras el editor de esquemáticos y el c: You close the schematic editor and the chat writes the `.kicad_sch`, with a copy in `.kicad-ia-backup/`.
En KiCad pasas a la placa con **F8**: He: In KiCad you move to the board with **F8**: Tools → Update PCB from Schematic.
Si quieres, pides organizar, colocar o a: If you want, you ask it to organize, place or autoroute. Place and autoroute show the proposal and are applied when you confirm.
Diagrama de bloques: editor de PCB, chat: Block diagram: PCB editor, chat, libraries, schematic, F8, then organize, place or autoroute
Colocar y autorutear no tocan la placa h: Place and autoroute do not touch the board until you confirm.
Las piezas salen de tus bibliotecas: The parts come from your libraries
El chat busca símbolos y huellas en `sym: The chat looks for symbols and footprints in `sym-lib-table` and `fp-lib-table`, the same tables you see in KiCad. If a part is not there, it does not draw another one in its place or invent a part number.
Antes de colocar nada, el chat fija por: Before placing anything, the chat writes down what you asked for: required components, forbidden ones and constraints. If a constraint cannot be checked against what the library says, it stays unknown and the chat asks you. A substitute never slips in silently: either you approve it or it is not used.
Un detalle fácil de pasar por alto: en l: A detail that is easy to miss: in the KiCad libraries, `Device:R`, `Device:C` and `Device:LED` come without a footprint. If the schematic is written like that, F8 leaves the part off the PCB.
Ahora la selección revisa la huella de c: Now the selection checks the footprint of every component. If the symbol has none, it proposes the ones in your library that match its filter and have as many pads as the symbol has pins. If there are several, it asks you. And the schematic writer has one last safeguard: a component without a footprint is not written. Power symbols, such as `GND`, do not need one.
Lo que ya está no se rehace: What is already there is not redone
Cada símbolo del esquemático tiene un id: Every schematic symbol has an identifier, and the footprint on the board stores that same id. If the chat deleted and redrew the symbol, the board would lose the link: F8 would see one new part and one left over.
Por eso, antes de escribir, el chat mira: So before writing, the chat looks at both the schematic and the board. A reference that already exists with the same symbol is kept with its id and position; only new parts are added. If the reference matches but the symbol is different, it does not swap it: it warns you. And if those references are already on the board, it refuses to redo the whole sheet.
El esquemático se escribe en el archivo: The schematic is written to the file
KiCad 10 tiene API para la placa, pero n: KiCad 10 has an API for the board, but not for the schematic. The plugin edits the `.kicad_sch` directly and, if the schematic editor has that file open, leaves it alone and asks you to close it. For the same reason, moving to the board is still your **F8**; the plugin does not import the netlist on its own.
En la placa, el chat puede organizar los: On the board, the chat can organize components by function, propose a placement and validate. When the board has no outline, it tells you which area to use or asks you to define one in `Edge.Cuts`, instead of guessing.
El autoruteo usa FreeRouting 2.0.1 con J: Autorouting uses FreeRouting 2.0.1 with Java 17 or later, and starts off. You turn it on in Settings together with the fabrication minimums: track width, clearance, via, drill and hole. The placement report is an IPC Class 2 pre-check, not a certification.
La barra de arriba dice si KiCad respond: The top bar says whether KiCad is responding, which model is selected and how many tokens have been used; if the provider does not report usage, it shows an estimate with `~`. On the left are the project, the PCB editor selection and your conversations: each one is saved on your computer, without the API key, and it only belongs to that project: it is read as a summary and cannot be continued.

Plugin para KiCad 10: describes el circu: A KiCad 10 plugin: you describe the circuit in a chat and the schematic comes out with the parts and footprints from your libraries.
Los bloques de siempre (un LED con su re: The usual blocks (an LED with its resistor, a regulator, a USB-C connector) get drawn again and again. KiCad IA builds them from one sentence, with the symbols and footprints you already have configured in KiCad. If a part is not there, it does not invent one.
Un chat local en Python que habla con Ki: A local Python chat that talks to KiCad 10 through its board API and writes the project's `.kicad_sch`, with a backup. The model can be Gemini, Ollama, OpenAI or any compatible URL.
Antes de escribir, fija lo que pediste y: Before writing, it pins down what you asked for and picks each part with a verified footprint. It keeps the components already on the schematic and the board, saves conversations, and proposes placement and autorouting with FreeRouting, applied when you confirm.
